why: The spelling, vocabulary and punctuation of the translation, revised by explicit editorial decisions. A word is respelt or modernized wherever the translation, its notes, and its front and back matter print it as a whole word. A verse's change is made to the words of that verse alone, which must have them once, and to the notes that quote them. Verses' changes stand in groups, each group under the reason its changes share. Each gives its reason. Passage changes name a stable note key or a front/back-matter unit and the plain words met once there; only punctuation, associated spacing and sentence-initial capitalization may change.

temporal clauses.why: Keep the time of an event distinct from present knowledge of it.

changes.why: The fourteen years date the catching up, not Paul's present knowledge of the man. Follow the RV comma placement while preserving the words and the intervening parenthesis.

rhetorical questions.why: Preserve the interrogative sentence that RP2026 prints.

changes.why: The question follows Jesus’ two questions in verse 17 and completes his reproach concerning the returning Samaritan.

RP2026 ends the question after λέγει, asking whether scripture speaks in vain, then independently asserts the spirit clause before the contrast with greater grace. The KJV boundary narrows the question to the quoted spirit statement; restore the target construction without resolving the difficult spirit/envy wording.
The spirit clause is an assertion once the question ends at vain; its stop follows the 1611 note on to envy, so it is revised apart from the question.

contextual-dashes.why: Set sentence endings and parenthetical continuations according to their syntax, preserving every word. Each decision names the pre-cleanup wording and its sentence structure.

changes.why: The invocation completes this sentence of Solomon's prayer; retain its full stop without a trailing dash.

changes.from: office,—even those from their cities, the men in each several city who were named expressly,—
changes.to: office (even those from their cities), the men in each several city who were named expressly
changes.why: The short qualification is parenthetical; the men named expressly continue the clause rather than form a second parenthesis. A separating space before the supplied were appointed preserves the word boundary formerly marked by the dash.

changes.from: Artaxerxes,—(this Artaxerxes ruled over a hundred and twenty-seven provinces from India)—
changes.to: Artaxerxes (this Artaxerxes ruled over a hundred and twenty-seven provinces from India),
changes.why: Parentheses already enclose the explanation of Artaxerxes; a comma resumes the surrounding sentence in the next verse.
The colon keeps the speech introduction connected to David's words in verse 3 across the parenthetical explanation of the Gabaonites; retain the parenthesis's lowercase opening.
The opening declaration of the prayer is a complete sentence; the next verse begins its supporting reason, For thou hast made the heaven and the earth.

changes.from: to the door,—to the door-post, and
changes.to: to the door, to the door-post, and
changes.why: The door-post specifies the door in the continuing instruction; a comma suffices.
The invocation ends here before the next verse begins a conditional sentence.
The comparison ends before the narrative identifies Balac; begin that narrative sentence with a capital.

before-em-dash.why: An em dash supplies the break marked by an adjacent comma, colon or semicolon. Remove only adjacent runs of these three marks before it in English; preserve periods (including abbreviation periods), question marks and exclamation marks. Sentence endings and contextual dash changes require explicit decisions.

preface-continuation.why: The three objects of consideration form one coordinated list; commas separate them without interrupting the parallel construction.

changes.from: original text,—of the fidelity of the version, and also,—of the correctness
changes.to: original text, of the fidelity of the version, and also of the correctness

reference-label-dashes.why: These appendix reference labels introduce their explanations with a dash; the period after the verse number is not an abbreviation or a sentence ending.

note-introduction-dashes.why: The dash introduces the explanation in these notes without ending a sentence; remove the ordinary period while retaining abbreviation periods.
